address: 上海市浦东新区龙阳路2345号
intro_zh: 上海新国际博览中心位于上海市浦东新区龙阳路2345号，处在浦东腹地、紧邻龙阳路交通枢纽，是上海会展业走向国际化的起点之一。展馆由上海陆家嘴展览发展有限公司与德国展览集团国际有限公司（成员包括德国汉诺威、杜塞尔多夫、慕尼黑三大展览公司）联合投资建造，是中国较早的中外合资展览中心，由美国Murphy/Jahn设计事务所设计。项目1999年11月4日培土奠基，2001年11月2日一期建成开放，此后历经十二期扩建，2012年2月15日全馆落成。场馆共17个单层无柱展厅，每个展厅70米×185米、面积11547平方米，室内展览面积20万平方米，室外展览面积10万平方米，另设3个入口大厅、20个卸货区和2个多层大型敞开式停车库及5个室外停车场。展馆以简洁、科学、经济为设计宗旨，标准化单元可灵活组合，被业内誉为最实用的展馆；每年举办约100余场知名展览会，吸引数百万海内外客商，是上海标志性建筑之一。交通依托地铁2号线、7号线与磁浮龙阳路站，可快速连接浦东国际机场、虹桥机场与市中心。
intro_en: Shanghai New International Expo Centre (SNIEC) is located at 2345 Longyang Road, Pudong New Area, in the heart of Pudong next to the Longyang Road transport hub, and marks one of the starting points of Shanghai's internationalisation in the exhibition business. It was jointly invested in and built by Shanghai Lujiazui Exhibition Development Co., Ltd. and Germany's Expo Group International, whose members are Hannover, Dusseldorf and Messe Munchen, making it one of China's earliest Sino-foreign joint-venture exhibition centres; the design came from the American firm Murphy/Jahn. Ground was broken on 4 November 1999, the first phase opened on 2 November 2001, and after twelve expansion stages the whole centre was completed on 15 February 2012. SNIEC has 17 single-storey pillar-free halls, each 70 by 185 metres and 11,547 square metres, giving 200,000 square metres indoors and 100,000 square metres outdoors, supported by three entrance halls, 20 loading docks, two multi-level open car parks and five surface car parks. Designed around simplicity, science and economy, its standardised modules combine flexibly and the venue is widely praised in the industry as the most practical exhibition centre in China; it hosts roughly 100 well-known exhibitions a year, draws millions of trade visitors and counts as one of Shanghai's landmark buildings. Metro Lines 2 and 7 and the Maglev share Longyang Road station, linking Pudong and Hongqiao airports with the city centre.

address: 长沙市长沙县黄兴镇浏阳河东岸
intro_zh: 长沙国际会展中心位于长沙市长沙县黄兴镇浏阳河东岸，处在湖南自贸区长沙片区会展区块，与长沙高铁南站隔河相望，是湖南省规模最大的专业展馆和长沙会展经济的“航空母舰”。项目2012年由湖南省委、省政府决策建设，2013年开工，一期2016年11月建成投运，占地约800亩，按重工业展和专业展会标准设计。场馆规划12个单层展馆、6个连接厅及南北两个登录厅，总建筑面积约43.3万平方米，其中地上约30.1万平方米，室内净展示面积约17.75万平方米，室外净展示面积约8.5万平方米，单个展厅面积约1.35万至1.45万平方米；一期含8个单层展馆、4个连接厅与北登录厅，室内展览面积11.4万平方米，可提供约6000个国际标准展位，二期续建南登录厅与南面4个展馆。开馆以来承接中非经贸博览会、长沙国际工程机械展、全国糖酒会、全国制药机械博览会、中国畜牧业博览会等品牌展会，是湖南首家通过UFI认证的场馆。场馆紧邻京港澳、沪昆、绕城等高速，距黄花国际机场约15公里，有4条地铁线汇入片区。
intro_en: Changsha International Convention and Exhibition Center lies on the east bank of the Liuyang River in Huangxing Town, Changsha County, within the exhibition block of the Hunan Pilot Free Trade Zone's Changsha area, facing Changsha South high-speed railway station across the river. Decided by the Hunan provincial party committee and government in 2012 and begun in 2013, it is the largest professional exhibition venue in Hunan and has been called the aircraft carrier of Changsha's exhibition economy. Phase one was completed and opened in November 2016 on about 800 mu of land, designed to heavy-industry and professional trade-show standards. The master plan provides 12 single-storey halls, six link halls and north and south registration halls, with about 433,000 square metres of floor area, of which some 301,000 square metres are above ground; net indoor exhibition space is about 177,500 square metres and outdoor space about 85,000 square metres, each hall measuring roughly 13,500 to 14,500 square metres. Phase one comprises eight halls, four link halls and the north registration hall, offering 114,000 square metres indoors and about 6,000 international standard booths, while phase two adds the south registration hall and four southern halls. Since opening it has hosted the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo, the Changsha International Construction Equipment Exhibition, the National Sugar and Wine Fair and the China Animal Husbandry Expo, and was the first venue in Hunan to gain UFI certification.

name_zh: 中铁·长春东北亚国际博览中心
address: 吉林省长春市朝阳区永春街777号
intro_zh: 中铁·长春东北亚国际博览中心位于长春市朝阳区中铁·长春博览城，距市政府约5公里，是长春国际会展中心2025年展馆退场后接棒的城市新会展平台，也是吉林省对外展示与招商的重要窗口。项目由中铁投资建设，博览城总投资约400亿元、总建筑面积450万平方米，集展览、会议、餐饮、旅游、酒店、商业与写字楼于一体。主体由占地34.2万平方米的东北亚国际展览中心、4.4万平方米的国际会议中心和4.5万平方米的酒店组成。展览中心一期19.4万平方米，包含3个标准展厅、多功能展厅、东登录厅、交通连廊与地下车库；净展览面积16.7万平方米，其中室内净展10.7万平方米、室外6万平方米，可提供8585个国际标准展位。2024年6月落成开业，当年即承接长春国际光电博览会、高等教育博览会与第十五届中国—东北亚博览会等大型展会。特色是展厅标准化程度高、室外展场充裕，展与会、酒店同园区。交通上经长春绕城高速与硅谷大街连接主城，距长春西站约12公里、龙嘉国际机场约35公里。展览中心已投用的一期含 A1、A2、A3 三个标准展厅与 C 多功能展厅：A1–A3 各 85 米×218 米、净高 12 米、净展 18,500 平方米、地面承重 3.5 吨/平方米、可设 965 个标准展位，配会议室与贵宾室 10 间、单馆电量总负荷 3,000 千瓦；C 厅 100 米×161 米、净高 14 米、净展 16,000 平方米、可设 1,065 个标准展位、配 13 间会议室贵宾室、1,600 千瓦。A3 厅内有 4 根直径 1.1 米的柱子，其余三厅为单层无柱。
intro_en: China Railway Northeast Asia International Expo Center is located in the China Railway Changchun Expo City in Chaoyang District, about five kilometres from the municipal government. It is the platform that took over the city's exhibition business as the halls of Changchun International Convention and Exhibition Center were retired in 2025, and it serves as Jilin Province's key window for trade promotion. Developed by China Railway with total investment of about RMB 40 billion and 4.5 million sqm of floor area across the Expo City, the project combines exhibition, conference, dining, tourism, hotel, retail and office uses. Its core comprises the 342,000 sqm Northeast Asia International Exhibition Center, a 44,000 sqm international conference centre and a 45,000 sqm hotel. Phase 1 of the exhibition centre covers 194,000 sqm with three standard halls, a multipurpose hall, the east registration hall, connecting corridors and underground parking; net exhibition area is 167,000 sqm, of which 107,000 sqm is indoor and 60,000 sqm outdoor, accommodating 8,585 standard booths. Opened in June 2024, it hosted the Changchun International Optoelectronics Expo, the Higher Education Expo and the 15th China-Northeast Asia Expo within its first seasons. Standardised halls, generous outdoor space and an on-site hotel distinguish the venue. The ring expressway and Guigu Avenue link it to the city centre, about 12 km from Changchun West Railway Station and 35 km from Longjia International Airport. Phase one, already open, has three standard halls (A1–A3, each 85 m by 218 m, 12 m clear height, 18,500 sqm, 3.5 t/sqm floor load, 965 booths, 10 meeting and VIP rooms, 3,000 kW) and the C multi-purpose hall (100 m by 161 m, 14 m clear height, 16,000 sqm, 1,065 booths, 13 rooms, 1,600 kW); A3 has four 1.1 m columns, the others are column-free.
source: cnexpo.com/venue/501；ccchaoyang.gov.cn 2023-06；jl.xinhuanet.com 2025-11 报道；liumosu/好展会网；聚展/会展网场馆页；地址补正：第63届高博会通知（教育部批准）载「永春镇兴博路777号」；团队 2026-10-27 整理《国际展览中心各展厅参数一览表》；地址以团队 2026-10-27 整理为准：朝阳区永春街777号（此前据高博会通知记「永春镇兴博路777号」，同址不同路名写法）

name_zh: 贵阳国际会议展览中心
address: 贵州省贵阳市观山湖区林城东路与长岭南路交叉口
intro_zh: 贵阳国际会议展览中心位于贵阳市观山湖区，紧邻市级行政中心与观山湖公园，是贵阳对外经贸活动的核心窗口，也是贵州省内功能最完整的会展综合体。项目由中天城投集团投资建设并运营，总建筑面积100万平方米，包含国际会议展览中心、国际生态会议中心、中天凯悦酒店、中天201中心、创意SOHO、美食城与地下停车场等，形成会展、酒店、商业、办公复合业态。展览中心建筑面积28万平方米，可用于展出的面积12万平方米，由8个展厅、1个登录大厅和4万平方米室外广场组成，可设6000个国际标准展位。会议中心逾4万平方米，设3500人大型会议厅、3000人宴会厅与500人国际会议厅。特色是绿色生态技术集成，2012年7月获LEED-NC铂金奖，为西南地区唯一。交通上经林城东路、观山东路连接老城与贵遵高速，距贵阳北站约8公里、龙洞堡国际机场约25公里，地铁1号线观山湖片区可达。本库已收录 1 至 8 号展厅与登录大厅共 9 条厅位数据，净展面积合计约 7.66 万平方米。
intro_en: Guiyang International Conference and Exhibition Center stands at 1 Changling North Road in Guanshanhu District, beside the municipal administrative centre and Guanshanhu Park. It is the city's front door for trade and investment and the most complete exhibition and conference complex in Guizhou. Zhongtian Urban Development Group invested in, built and operates the project; it was completed at the end of 2010 and opened in early 2011. The estate totals 1 million sqm of floor area and is deliberately mixed-use. The exhibition centre, an international eco conference centre, the Zhongtian Hyatt hotel, the Zhongtian 201 tower, creative SOHO units, a food street and underground parking all sit inside one cluster, so a show can be staged, hosted and accommodated without leaving the site. The exhibition centre accounts for 280,000 sqm of that, with 120,000 sqm usable for exhibitions. It is arranged as eight halls, a single registration hall and a 40,000 sqm outdoor plaza, and can be laid out for 6,000 standard booths. The conference centre exceeds 40,000 sqm and holds a 3,500-seat plenary hall, a 3,000-seat banquet hall and a 500-seat international conference hall, which is why it can hold a trade fair and a summit at the same time. That is how it is used in practice: the China International Big Data Industry Expo, the world's first expo devoted to big data, has run here since 2015, alongside the Eco Forum Global Guiyang and the Guizhou liquor fair. Architecturally the complex is less a single object than a green-technology testbed, assembled by a group of international design teams and green-building consultants rather than one hand; the halls, the conference block, the hotel and the office tower stand as separate volumes on one estate, with the 40,000 sqm outdoor plaza between them. Energy-saving, water-recycling and low-carbon systems were written into the design from the start, and in July 2012 the project received LEED-NC Platinum, the only rating of its kind in southwest China at the time. Transport is straightforward. Lincheng East and Guanshan East roads link the district to the old city and the Guizun expressway, and Metro Line 1 stops at International Eco Conference Center station, opened in December 2017, at the northeast corner of the site. Guiyang North Railway Station is about 8 km away and Longdongbao International Airport about 25 km.
source: liumosu；zwhz；cnexpo；贵阳市观山湖区公开资料

name_zh: 济南黄河国际会展中心
address: 山东省济南市新旧动能转换起步区崔寨组团
intro_zh: 济南黄河国际会展中心位于山东省济南市新旧动能转换起步区崔寨组团，是济南跨河北上的标志性会展项目，也是起步区最先落成的大型公共设施之一，承担着带动黄河北岸产业与城市功能集聚的作用。项目由法国VP建筑设计事务所设计，2020年中标、2023年11月一期正式投入使用，由东向西分为展览中心、会议中心和酒店中心三大板块，整体形态取意“黄河画卷”。全部建成后总建筑面积约120万平方米，净展览面积可达51万平方米，其中一期建筑面积约37.3万平方米；按规划口径为全球净展面积领先的会展中心之一。展馆为大跨度无柱设计，可灵活分隔组合，适配智能制造、机床、工业装备等重型展会。建筑以舒展的曲线屋面呼应黄河意向，会议中心如桥梁横跨于画卷之上。交通上紧邻京沪高速与济南绕城高速，距济南东站约20公里、遥墙国际机场约25公里，起步区内部道路体系与轨道交通正在完善。
intro_en: Jinan Yellow River International Convention and Exhibition Center sits in the Cuizhai cluster of the city's New and Old Kinetic Energy Conversion Start Zone, on the north bank of the Yellow River. It took Jinan's exhibition industry across the river, as one of the first large public buildings to open in the start zone and the anchor around which industry and urban functions are gathering on the north side. France's VP Architecture won the design competition in 2020 and Phase 1 opened in November 2023, when the China (Jinan) International Machine Tool and Intelligent Manufacturing Equipment Expo brought more than 500 exhibitors into the halls. The masterplan runs west to east through three blocks — exhibition centre, conference centre and hotel centre — and takes the Yellow River scroll painting as its organising image: long curved roofs, with the conference centre reading as a bridge laid across the scroll. Later phases are still being built out. On completion the total floor area will be about 1.2 million sqm with net exhibition space of 510,000 sqm, which would place it among the largest exhibition centres in the world on that measure; Phase 1 alone is 373,000 sqm. What Phase 1 already delivers is heavy-industry capability. Twelve standard halls, a large N1 hall and a registration hall give roughly 150,000 sqm of indoor exhibition space, all single-storey and large-span with no internal columns, and a floor load rating of 5 tonnes per sqm. That is the specification machine tools, industrial equipment and intelligent manufacturing shows need, and the halls can be subdivided when a smaller event takes only part of the building. Road access is the easy part. The site adjoins the Beijing-Shanghai expressway and the Jinan ring expressway, about 20 km from Jinan East Railway Station and 25 km from Yaoqiang International Airport. Streets and rail links inside the start zone are still filling in, so for now most visitors arrive by car or coach.

name_zh: 北京九华国际会展中心
address: 北京市昌平区小汤山镇
intro_zh: 北京九华国际会展中心位于北京市昌平区小汤山镇，东临首都国际机场、南靠温榆河生态走廊，是京北地区依托度假酒店群发展起来的会展综合体，填补了北京北部大型展会的场地空白。场馆隶属九华山庄，是国内较早采用“会展+温泉度假酒店”模式的场馆之一，把展览、会议、住宿、餐饮、温泉、体检等功能集中在一个园区内。展馆室内展览面积约5万平方米，由多个单元展厅组成，另有可分隔的会议厅与宴会厅，适合消费类展会、行业年会、企业订货会与培训活动。特色是展馆与五星级度假酒店零距离接驳，参展与住宿一体化，停车位充足，适合多日活动与家庭型消费展。建筑为低层庭院式布局，与山庄园林和温泉区相连，风格偏度假而非城市展馆。交通上通过京承高速、京藏高速、六环路与立汤路连接市区，距首都机场约20公里，园区提供机场巴士与大量停车位，公共交通以公交和出租车为主。
intro_en: Beijing Jiuhua International Exhibition Center lies in Xiaotangshan, Changping District, with Capital International Airport to the east and the Wenyu River ecological corridor to the south. It was built to fill the gap in large-scale exhibition space in northern Beijing, and it did so not as a city-centre hall but as exhibition space attached to a resort. It belongs to Jiuhua Resort and was among the first venues in China to pair exhibition halls with a hot-spring resort hotel, the model that still defines it. Exhibition, conference, accommodation, dining, spa, medical check-up and shopping functions share one estate instead of being spread across a city, and that single-site arrangement is the whole proposition. A consumer fair, an industry annual meeting, a dealer conference or a training programme can run for several days with the same people sleeping, eating and meeting within walking distance of the stands. The site covers 622,000 sqm. The main hall building occupies 96,000 sqm of ground, temporary hall space a further 63,000 sqm, and there is 120,000 sqm of outdoor exhibition yard, enough for plant, vehicles and outdoor demonstrations. Indoors, about 50,000 sqm of exhibition space is arranged across three interconnected halls — A, B and C — on a single level, with combined registration areas of nearly 9,600 sqm, and divisible conference and banquet rooms alongside them. Architecturally it reads as a resort rather than an exhibition centre. Buildings are low-rise and courtyard-based, opening onto the gardens and the spa area, and the scale stays human rather than monumental. Access is by road: the Jingcheng and Jingzang expressways, the Sixth Ring Road and Litang Road all feed the site, which is about 20 km from Capital Airport. The resort runs an airport shuttle, and outdoor parking alone covers 250,000 sqm. Public transport otherwise means buses and taxis, which is the trade-off for a site that can hold a multi-day event end to end.

name_zh: 广东现代国际展览中心
address: 广东省东莞市厚街镇家具大道2号
intro_zh: 广东现代国际展览中心位于东莞市厚街镇，处在粤港澳大湾区中轴与广深科创走廊中部，是东莞依托“国际制造基地”产业基础建成的专业展馆，也是华南地区最早一批面向制造业的民营会展场馆之一。运营公司成立于2000年12月，场馆占地33万平方米，现有5个展览馆，室内展览面积约10万至13万平方米（不同年份口径），室外展场约8万至9万平方米，可提供5500至7000余个国际标准展位，是亚洲单体面积较大的展馆之一。特色是90米跨度无柱空间与可自由分隔的展区，配11间85至2400平方米会议室及带伸缩舞台的2400平方米多功能厅，适合机械、家具、鞋机鞋材、电子等东莞优势产业展会。建筑采用索网结构屋顶，通过空中走廊连接嘉华大酒店，形成展贸一体综合体。交通上紧邻广深高速厚街出口与莞太路，距虎门高铁站约15公里、深圳宝安机场约40公里。本库已收录序厅与 A、B、C、D、E 五个展区（含 E2 区）共 7 条厅位数据，标准展区地面承重约 5 吨/平方米、序厅约 0.5 吨/平方米。
intro_en: Guangdong Modern International Exhibition Center occupies 330,000 sqm at 1 Furniture Avenue, Houjie, Dongguan, in the middle of the Greater Bay Area and on the Guangzhou-Shenzhen innovation corridor. It was built by a private operator for the manufacturing base around it — the company was founded in December 2000, the halls opened in 2002 and it joined UFI in 2004 — which makes it one of the earliest privately run, industry-facing venues in South China. When it was planned, the argument was size: the first-phase main hall of more than 70,000 sqm was promoted as the largest single exhibition hall in China. Today the site holds five halls, with indoor exhibition space of roughly 100,000 to 130,000 sqm depending on which year's figure is used, and 80,000 to 90,000 sqm outdoors. That supports 5,500 to over 7,000 standard booths, and the venue is usually counted among Asia's larger single-site exhibition grounds. The engineering suits the trades it serves. The main structure spans 90 m without columns and the floor divides into zones of different sizes, so a furniture fair, a shoe-machinery show and an electronics expo can run side by side without temporary walls fighting the roof. Eleven meeting rooms range from 85 to 2,400 sqm, and the 2,400 sqm multipurpose hall has a retractable stage for launches and ceremonies. The roof is a cable-net structure, an unusual choice for a hall of this age, and an elevated walkway links the halls to the Jiahua Hotel, so buyers and exhibitors move between stand and room without going outside. That is the exhibition-and-trade arrangement Houjie's furniture and footwear industries were built on, and a third phase of expansion began in 2023. Transport: the site sits at the Houjie exit of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen expressway, off Guantai Road, about 15 km from Humen high-speed rail station and 40 km from Shenzhen Bao'an Airport.
source: baike.baidu.com/广东现代国际展览中心；gde.cc；are-expo；场馆公开资料（家具大道2号）

address: 湖北省武汉市汉阳区鹦鹉大道619号
intro_zh: 武汉国际博览中心位于武汉市汉阳区四新组团滨江地带，东临长江江滩、南至三环线，是华中地区规模最大的会展综合体，也是武汉新区开发的核心项目之一。项目2006年12月开工，规划用地1.58平方公里、总建筑面积约240万平方米，总投资约78.3亿元，自西向东分为会展、会议、酒店三大区域，一期展馆工程总建筑面积约47万平方米、投资约20亿元。室内展览面积12.6万平方米，由A1至A6、B1至B6共12个展馆组成，每馆约72米×117米，设4个货运门，其中2个高7米、2个高4.5米，适合大型设备进出。特色是展馆体量均衡、可整馆连通使用，配套洲际酒店、会议中心与商业。建筑以连续弧形屋面沿江展开。交通上经鹦鹉大道、三环线与杨泗港长江大桥连接武昌、汉口，距武汉站约25公里、天河机场约35公里，地铁6号线可达。本库已收录 A1 至 A6、B1 至 B6 共 12 个展厅的逐厅数据。场馆由 12 个主馆、10 个连接馆与 2 个登录厅组成，室内展览面积约 15 万平方米、室外约 4 万平方米，展览总面积约 19 万平方米，可设约 6,880 个标准展位；主馆单馆约 8,500 平方米、净高约 17.5 米，连接馆净高约 11 米，单馆供电容量约 3,500 千瓦，配停车位约 2,864 个。
intro_en: Wuhan International Expo Center occupies the riverside Si Xin cluster in Hanyang District, bordering the Yangtze floodplain to the east and the Third Ring Road to the south. It is the largest exhibition complex in central China and a core project of Wuhan's new district. Construction began in December 2006 on a 1.58 sq km site with about 2.4 million sqm of total floor area and investment of roughly RMB 7.83 billion, organised west to east into exhibition, conference and hotel zones; the Phase 1 halls total about 470,000 sqm of floor area at a cost of some RMB 2 billion. Indoor exhibition space is 126,000 sqm across 12 halls, A1 to A6 and B1 to B6, each about 72 by 117 m, with four freight doors of which two are 7 m high and two 4.5 m, allowing large equipment access. Evenly sized halls can be combined as a whole, supported by an InterContinental hotel, conference centre and retail. A continuous curved roof runs along the river. The site connects via Yingwu Avenue, the Third Ring Road and Yangsigang Yangtze Bridge, about 25 km from Wuhan Railway Station and 35 km from Tianhe Airport, with Metro Line 6 nearby. Counting the 10 connecting halls and two registration halls, the complex offers about 150,000 sqm indoors and 40,000 sqm outdoors — some 190,000 sqm in total and about 6,880 standard booths. Main halls measure about 8,500 sqm at a 17.5 m clear height, connecting halls 11 m, each hall has roughly 3,500 kW of power, and about 2,864 parking spaces serve the site.

name_zh: 中国·红岛国际会议展览中心
address: 青岛市城阳区火炬路326号的红岛高新区
intro_zh: 中国·红岛国际会议展览中心位于青岛市城阳区火炬路326号的红岛高新区，是青岛“双馆运营”格局中的新馆，与崂山老馆共同承载青岛会展业，也是山东规模最大的会展经济综合体之一。场馆由中国建研院与德国gmp国际建筑设计有限公司联合设计，投资约67亿元，2019年5月竣工开馆，由青岛国信红岛国际会议展览中心有限公司运营。总建筑面积48.8万平方米，设14个展厅，总展览面积14万平方米，定位为展览、会议、酒店、办公与商业一体的综合体。特色是H型对称布局与40米高入口大厅，入口采用跨度93米的张拉膜结构、天然采光玻璃屋面；展厅东西向阵列，荷载与净高适合装备制造类展会。交通上经胶州湾高速、环湾大道与火炬路连接青岛主城，距胶东国际机场约30公里、青岛北站约20公里，周边停车配套充足。本库已收录西侧 4 个展厅、东侧首层 5 个展厅与东侧二层 5 个展厅，共 14 条逐厅数据。
intro_en: The Hongdao International Conference and Exhibition Center occupies a 488,000 sqm site at 326 Huoju Road in the Hongdao high-tech zone of Chengyang District, Qingdao, making it the largest exhibition complex in Shandong. It is the newer half of the city's two-venue arrangement: the older Laoshan hall by the coast still runs, and the two are worked as a pair. Designed jointly by the China Academy of Building Research and Germany's gmp, it was built in 22 months for about RMB 6.7 billion and opened on 15 May 2019, operated by Qingdao Guoxin Hongdao International Conference and Exhibition Center Co. The brief was what the Chinese industry calls a fifth-generation complex — exhibition, conference, hotel, office and retail under one roof rather than halls with offices next door. The building runs 17 storeys above ground and three below, with hotel towers at its north and south ends. The plan is a symmetrical H. A 40 m high entrance hall sits on the north-south axis under a 93 m span tensile membrane and naturally lit glazing, and the exhibition wings run east and west from it. The west wing holds four single-storey halls with 18 m clear height and no columns, which is what large plant and equipment needs; the east wing stacks ten halls over two levels, five with columns at ground floor and a column-free upper deck. That double-deck section has its own first-floor loading and separate logistics and visitor routes, so an articulated lorry and a delegate group never meet. In total there are 14 halls and 140,000 sqm of exhibition space. Access runs through the Jiaozhou Bay expressway, Huanwan Avenue and Huoju Road, about 30 km from Jiaodong International Airport and 20 km from Qingdao North Railway Station, with parking on site. The airport distance is the weak point: this is a suburban site and visitors should plan on road transfer rather than rail.

name_zh: 中国国际展览中心（朝阳馆）
address: 北京市朝阳区北三环东路静安庄
intro_zh: 中国国际展览中心（朝阳馆）位于北京市朝阳区北三环东路静安庄，是新中国成立后由国家批准建设的第一座大型专业展馆，1985年10月建成，被评为北京80年代十大建筑之一，被视为中国现代展览业的起点，此后长期承担国家级经贸展览与涉外展会。场馆隶属中国国际展览中心集团（中国贸促会直属企业）。占地约15万平方米，拥有8个展馆、室内外展出面约6万平方米，其中1号馆主体建筑面积超过5万平方米，是国内面积最大的老馆之一；结构体系包含网架、钢筋混凝土与钢结构三种形式。特色是1号馆的标志性方形体量与中央庭院，展馆分布紧凑、动线短，适合消费品、礼品、轻工与专业展。交通上紧邻北三环与京承高速，地铁10号线三元桥站、13号线光熙门站步行可达，距首都机场约20公里。本库已收录 1 至 8 号馆共 14 条厅位数据（1 号馆按 A/B 段与楼层拆分、8 号馆按 A/B 段拆分），厅内净展面积合计约 5.3 万平方米。
intro_en: The China International Exhibition Center's Chaoyang venue occupies 15 hectares at 6 North Third Ring Road East, Jing'anzhuang, in Chaoyang District, Beijing. It is the founding address of the China International Exhibition Center and the first large purpose-built exhibition hall approved by the state after 1949, completed in October 1985, listed among Beijing's top ten buildings of the 1980s, and generally treated as the point where China's modern exhibition industry begins. Its opening event, the Asia-Pacific International Trade Fair, set the pattern for three decades of national trade fairs and international exhibitions, and the venue has carried that role ever since. It belongs to the China International Exhibition Center Group, under the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade. The Beijing Institute of Architectural Design laid it out on a compact plan that predates the standards now applied to new halls. Eight halls hold about 60,000 sqm of indoor exhibition space and a further 7,000 sqm outdoors, with a 16,000 sqm car park. Hall 1, the main building, is the largest single structure on site at more than 50,000 sqm of gross floor area — a figure covering the whole building rather than stand space alone — and ranks among the biggest of China's older exhibition buildings. Three structural systems coexist — space frame, reinforced concrete and steel — a record of how the site was added to over time. Hall 1's square massing and central courtyard set the tone, and the annexes wrap around it: Halls 2 to 5 run together along the Third Ring, Halls 6 and 7 are joined on the north-west side, and Hall 8 stands alone to the south-west. That tight plan is the practical advantage. Walking distances are short, halls connect without going outside, and the whole site can be worked in a day, which is why it still suits consumer goods, gifts, light industry and specialist trade fairs rather than the capital-goods shows that moved to Shunyi. Transport is unusually good for a venue of this age: the North Third Ring Road and the Jingcheng expressway are at the gate, Sanyuanqiao on Metro Line 10 and Guangximen on Line 13 are within walking distance, and Capital Airport is about 20 km away.

address: 山东省临沂市商谷示范区
intro_zh: 临沂国际博览中心位于山东省临沂市商谷示范区，由临沂商城国际贸易集团有限公司投资建设，是鲁南苏北地区重要的会展平台，对临沂这座“中国市场名城”“物流之都”以展会带动商贸物流升级具有关键作用。场馆总建筑面积约9.5万平方米，其中地上约4.1万平方米、地下约5.4万平方米，整体采用钢框架结构，使建筑与结构、设计与功能更加一体化，馆内空间布局规整，集展览、会议、办公等多种业态于一体。临沂地处鲁南苏北中心位置，交通便利、物流网络发达，场馆可辐射山东南部、江苏北部及周边区域，承接中国（临沂）国际商贸物流博览会等品牌展会。展馆以现代化智能场馆标准建设，货运流线与商贸集散需求匹配，是区域商贸物流与会展融合的重要节点。建筑整体形象如一艘起航的航艇，立面采用弧状、变化的百叶格栅，取“沂水潺潺、波光荡漾”之意，体量自下而上层层收束，形成向上的动感与腾飞之势；作为临沂商谷示范区的前期配套项目，博览中心率先建成并带动整个片区启动。
intro_en: Linyi International Expo and Exhibition Center occupies a site in the Shanggu Demonstration Zone of Linyi, Shandong, and was invested in by Linyi Mall International Trade Group. It is one of the most important exhibition platforms for southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu and plays a central role in Linyi's strategy of using trade fairs to upgrade its wholesale and logistics economy, in a city long known as a national market city and logistics capital. The complex has about 95,000 sqm of total floor area, of which roughly 41,000 sqm is above ground and 54,000 sqm below, and is built with a steel-frame structure that integrates architecture with engineering and design with function. Interior layouts are orderly and regular, combining exhibition halls, conference facilities and office space so that a single visit can cover exhibiting, meeting and business negotiation. Linyi sits at the geographical centre of southern Shandong and northern Jiangsu, with convenient road links and a dense logistics network, which allows the venue to draw exhibitors and buyers from Shandong, Jiangsu, Anhui and Henan. Its regular calendar includes flagship events such as the China (Linyi) International Trade and Logistics Expo, reflecting the city's strength in wholesale markets, warehousing and distribution. The venue was built to modern intelligent-building standards, with freight routes and loading areas designed around the needs of trade and logistics distribution rather than one-off consumer shows. That combination of a trade-city hinterland, underground parking and service space, and direct freight access makes it a key node where regional commerce and exhibitions meet. The building reads as a ship setting out: a curved, varying louvre screen wraps the facade in an echo of the Yi River's rippling water, and the massing steps inward as it rises to give an upward, lifting profile. As the first supporting project of the Shanggu Demonstration Zone, the centre was completed ahead of the district and set its development in motion.

address: 3-11-1 Ariake, Koto-ku, Tokyo 135-0063, Japan
intro_en: Tokyo Big Sight, officially the Tokyo International Exhibition Center, occupies a site of about 243,000 sqm at 3-11-1 Ariake in Koto-ku, on the Tokyo Bay waterfront in the Ariake Minami district of Tokyo Waterfront City. It opened on 1 April 1996 and is Japan's largest exhibition complex; its operator states plainly that the three exhibition buildings together hold the country's largest indoor exhibition area. The venue sits at the centre of Tokyo's event economy, hosting Comiket twice a year, AnimeJapan and major trade fairs, and during the Tokyo 2020 Games it served as the main press and broadcast centre after organisers moved sports events elsewhere to cut costs.  The complex contains 16 exhibition halls in three buildings - East Halls 1 to 8, West Halls 1 to 4 and South Halls 1 to 4, the last opened in July 2019 - plus the Conference Tower, which houses a 1,000-seat International Conference Room, a 1,700 sqm Reception Hall and 22 meeting rooms ranging from 35 to 760 sqm. Support space includes show offices, dressing rooms, a service corner and a conference support centre.  Indoor exhibition area totals 115,420 sqm, with a further 6,000 sqm on the roof and a total floor area of 316,990 sqm. Individual halls run from 3,080 sqm to 11,680 sqm (East Hall 7, the largest); East Halls 1 to 6 each measure 90 by 90 m, and movable partitions let three of them merge into a single floor of about 25,000 sqm. Ceilings reach 31 m, floor loading is 5 tonnes per sqm in the main halls, and the 600 m East Galleria carries moving walkways, restaurants and service points.  Architecturally the site is defined by AXS Satow's Conference Tower, an eight-storey, 58 m structure of glass and titanium panels shaped as four inverted pyramids raised on concrete supports. Access is by the Yurikamome line to Tokyo Big Sight Station (about 3 minutes' walk) or the Rinkai Line to Kokusai-Tenjijo Station (about 7 minutes), roughly 30 minutes by rail from Tokyo Station.

address: 2-1, Nakase, Mihama-ku, Chiba-city, 261-8550, Japan
intro_en: Makuhari Messe, formally the Nippon Convention Center, stands at 2-1 Nakase in Mihama-ku, Chiba City, on the reclaimed waterfront of Makuhari New City in Chiba Prefecture, roughly 30 km east of central Tokyo across Tokyo Bay. It opened on 9 October 1989 and is the second pillar of the Greater Tokyo exhibition market alongside Tokyo Big Sight, absorbing the region's largest consumer shows and trade fairs. Its calendar includes Tokyo Game Show, Tokyo Auto Salon, the biennial Tokyo Motor Show, Jump Festa and Summer Sonic, and during the Tokyo 2020 Olympics it hosted fencing, taekwondo, wrestling and goalball.  The venue is organised as an International Exhibition Hall of eleven halls, an International Conference Hall, and the Makuhari Event Hall with 7,860 seats. Exhibition Halls 1 to 8 are eight identical 6,750 sqm units arranged in a row and separated by movable partitions, so the whole block can be opened into a continuous 54,000 sqm floor. Exhibition Halls 9 to 11, added as the North Halls, add 18,000 sqm: Hall 9 at 9,000 sqm and Halls 10 and 11 at 4,500 sqm each. Indoor exhibition space therefore totals 72,000 sqm.  Each of Halls 1 to 8 measures 112.5 by 60 m with clear heights of 15 to 30 m and floor loading of 5 tonnes per sqm; Hall 9 measures 96 by 96 m with a 16 to 34 m ceiling. Organiser rooms, meeting rooms, show offices and loading access are attached to each block, and the site has extensive parking.  The complex was designed by Fumihiko Maki, the Pritzker laureate whose practice shaped the low, repetitive hall roofs and the waterfront setting of Makuhari New City. Access is easiest on the JR Keiyo Line to Kaihimmakuhari Station, about a 5-minute walk from the venue; by road it is roughly 40 minutes from central Tokyo or Haneda Airport and about 30 minutes from Narita Airport.

address: 1-5-102, Nanko-Kita, Suminoe-ku, Osaka 559-0034, Japan
intro_en: INTEX Osaka, officially the International Exhibition Center, Osaka, stands at 1-5-102 Nanko-Kita in Suminoe-ku, Osaka, on Sakishima Island in the Cosmosquare district of Osaka Bay - a planned business and trade zone linked to the city centre by metro and the Hanshin expressway network. It opened on 1 May 1985, with Hall 6 added in October 1993, and is the largest exhibition site in western Japan and the third largest in the country by exhibition space. Its standing in the region is reinforced by the events it has carried: the 2019 G20 Osaka Summit, Sibos 2012, the Osaka Motor Show and Osaka Auto Messe. The operator reports some 3,000 events and about 100 million visitors since opening.  The venue is built around six exhibition halls and a Center building, grouped around two public atriums known collectively as INTEX Plaza, which act as the circulation spine and event forecourt. Inside, the operator describes ten exhibition zones ranging from 5,000 to 10,000 sqm, several of them usable without pillars, so that shows can scale from a single hall to a full-site footprint. Total exhibition area is 72,978 sqm. Conference rooms, organiser offices and reception space sit in the Center building, and the atriums double as registration and catering areas.  The halls are clear-span structures with high roofs and vehicle access at grade, which is what allows heavy machinery, vehicles and large-scale food equipment shows to move in directly. The modular zoning is the feature the operator markets most heavily, because it lets a mid-sized show avoid paying for a full hall.  Access is straightforward: Nakafuto Station on the Osaka Metro Nanko Port Town Line is about a 5-minute walk away, Trade Center-mae Station about 8 to 9 minutes, and Cosmosquare Station about 10 minutes. The site is also served by buses and has on-site parking, and it sits about 30 to 40 minutes by road from central Osaka.

address: 2-2 Kinjofuto, Minato-ku, Nagoya 455-0848, Japan（愛知県名古屋市港区金城ふ頭二丁目2番地）
intro_en: Port Messe Nagoya, formally the Nagoya International Exhibition Hall, occupies reclaimed land at Nagoya Port in Minato-ku, Nagoya, at 2-2 Kinjo-futo. Its history as a trade-fair site dates to 1973, making it one of the earliest purpose-built exhibition locations in central Japan, and it remains the principal venue for the manufacturing and automotive supply chains of Aichi Prefecture. Shows such as Manufacturing World Nagoya and the mechatronics technology exhibitions use it as their regional home, drawing exhibitors from the Toyota production network and the wider Chubu industrial belt.  The complex comprises three exhibition halls plus a Convention Hall, an Event Hall and a Main Hall with seven meeting rooms of various sizes for seminars and scientific meetings. Exhibition Hall 1, completed in October 2022, is the newest and largest element: 20,000 sqm of pillar-free floor with a 20 m ceiling, divisible into four sections by movable partitions. Hall 2 offers 6,576 sqm of pillar-free space with large shutters on two sides for fast build-up and dismantling, and Hall 3 is a square pillar-free hall of up to 13,500 sqm that can be split into quarters of 4,050 sqm. Indoor exhibition space therefore totals roughly 40,000 sqm.  The Convention Hall adds about 1,300 sqm of conference and banquet space with halls of 1,000 and 300 sqm that also divide into four, and it is placed at the centre of the site as a physical nexus between the three exhibition halls. The Event Hall has four simultaneous interpretation booths and can be partitioned.  Access runs on the Aonami Line to Kinjo-futo Station, about a 5-minute walk from the halls and roughly 24 minutes from Nagoya Station; taxis take about 30 to 40 minutes from the station, and the port location puts the halls close to the city's expressway network.

address: 7-1 Okihama-machi, Hakata-ku, Fukuoka City, Japan
intro_en: Marine Messe Fukuoka sits on the Hakata Bay waterfront at 7-1 Okihama-machi in Hakata-ku, Fukuoka, within the city's concentrated convention zone alongside the Fukuoka International Congress Center and the Fukuoka Kokusai Center. Hall A opened in 1994 and was the venue for the 1995 Summer Universiade, which is why the building combines an arena, an exhibition floor and a concert hall in one envelope. It is the largest arena-scale facility in Kyushu and has hosted the 2001 and 2023 World Aquatics Championships, volleyball and basketball championships, and arena tours by major Japanese and Korean artists.  Hall A is a multipurpose structure: its arena floor of about 8,000 sqm doubles as exhibition space of roughly 9,100 sqm, and the seated capacity reaches 15,000 for sport and about 13,000 for concerts. Hall B, opened in 2019 as a second-phase exhibition building at 2-1 Okihama-machi, adds a 5,000 sqm pillar-free multipurpose exhibition room with a capacity of 6,000, modern utility supply, ceiling-suspended rigging points and dimming equipment. Together the two halls give Fukuoka a combined exhibition and arena offer that no other city in Kyushu matches, and they are operated as one complex with the congress centre by the Fukuoka Convention Center Foundation.  The architecture is unmistakable from the water: the roof and facade are shaped after gulls wheeling over the bay, a form that also breaks up the mass of the arena behind it. Parking for about 1,200 visitor cars is available.  Access is by Nishitetsu bus from Hakata Station or Tenjin to the Marine Messe-mae stop, roughly 15 to 20 minutes, or by subway to Gofukumachi or Nakasu-Kawabata followed by a 17 to 18 minute walk; taxis from Hakata Station take about 15 minutes, and Fukuoka Airport is a short drive to the south.

address: 217-60 KINTEX-ro, Ilsanseo-gu, Goyang-si, Gyeonggi-do 10390, Republic of Korea（경기도 고양시 일산서구 킨텍스로 217-60）
intro_en: KINTEX, the Korea International Exhibition Center, stands at 217-60 Kintex-ro in Ilsanseo-gu, Goyang, Gyeonggi Province, about 23 km northwest of central Seoul on a 224,800 sqm site between Chungangno and the Han River. The first centre opened in April 2005 and the second in 2011, and together they make KINTEX the largest MICE venue in Korea and the only exhibition complex in the country with more than 100,000 sqm of indoor exhibition space. It anchors the western end of the Seoul metropolitan event market and is the main venue of the biennial Seoul Motor Show, as well as a regular host of KOTRA trade fairs, medical and technology congresses and large public examinations.  The complex is divided into two exhibition centres. Center 1 holds Halls 1 to 5, each about 171 by 63 m with a 15 m ceiling; Center 2 holds Halls 6 to 10, including Hall 6 at 5,580 sqm and the two largest halls, 9 and 10, at 13,238 and 13,072 sqm with 132 by 99 m floors and 15 m ceilings. Indoor exhibition area is 108,049 sqm, split almost evenly between the two centres at 53,541 and 54,508 sqm, with 2,849 sqm of outdoor space at Center 1 and 68,000 sqm at Center 2.  Support facilities include an event hall seating 6,000, 26 meeting rooms, a grand ballroom, organiser offices and loading docks. Floor loading is 5 tonnes per sqm in the main halls and 2 tonnes in Hall 6.  The main building is a three-storey structure, and the second centre was built with a large outdoor exhibition yard that can take construction equipment and vehicle demonstrations.  Access improved sharply with the GTX-A rapid line: KINTEX Station is about a 5-minute walk from the halls and puts Seoul Station roughly 20 minutes away. Seoul Metro Line 3 to Daehwa Station is a 10 to 15 minute walk or a short bus ride, and the site has extensive parking.

address: 513 Yeongdong-daero, Gangnam-gu, Seoul 06164, Republic of Korea
intro_en: COEX occupies the Korea World Trade Center complex at 513 Yeongdong-daero in Samseong-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, in the heart of the city's southern business district. Its history runs back to 1979, when the Korea Exhibition Center - KOEX - opened on the same block as the first permanent comprehensive exhibition hall in Korea, a 26,249 sqm building with one basement and three upper floors that was then the largest exhibition facility in the country. The present COEX was built ahead of the 1988 Seoul Olympics, and the ASEM Tower was completed on the old KOEX site in 2000 after the 1996 Asia-Europe Meeting confirmed Seoul as host. That lineage makes COEX the birthplace of the Korean MICE industry, and it has since carried the 2000 ASEM summit, the 2010 G20 Seoul summit and the 2012 Nuclear Security Summit.  The centre has four exhibition halls - A, B, C and D - with a combined 35,316 sqm, plus 55 meeting rooms, a 1,080-seat auditorium and the 3F Grand Ballroom of 1,972 sqm. Halls A and C are 10,368 sqm each on 144 by 72 m grids, Halls B and D 7,290 sqm each on 108 by 67.5 m grids, all at 10.5 m clear height and 1.5 tonnes per sqm floor loading. The halls connect directly to the COEX Mall, hotels and the Trade Tower, so a show can run without stepping outside.  The original KOEX translated traditional Korean timber framing into steel pipes and space trusses; the present complex is an underground and podium exhibition layer beneath a dense above-ground programme of offices, retail and convention space.  Access is exceptionally direct. Samseong Station on Seoul Metro Line 2 connects to COEX underground, and Bongeunsa Station on Line 9 serves the eastern side; both are within a few minutes' walk of the halls.

address: #55 APEC-ro, Haeundae-gu, Busan 48060, Republic of Korea
intro_en: BEXCO, the Busan Exhibition and Convention Center, stands at 55 APEC-ro in Haeundae-gu, Busan, at the centre of Centum City - a planned waterfront district of shopping malls, hotels, offices and cultural institutions on the city's eastern seafront. The operating corporation was founded on 5 December 1995, the building was completed on 23 May 2001 and it opened on 13 September 2001 as Korea's second purpose-built convention centre. It hosted the 2005 APEC summit, whose leaders met at the adjacent Nurimaru APEC House, and has since carried the 2012 Lions Clubs International Convention, the 2014 ITU Plenipotentiary Conference and the 10th Assembly of the World Council of Churches, cementing Busan's position as Korea's second MICE city.  The complex has two exhibition buildings. Exhibition Center 1 contains Halls 1, 2A, 2B, 3A and 3B: Hall 1 is 8,836 sqm on an 81 by 108 m grid with a 12.5 to 22.5 m ceiling, and the other four are 4,418 sqm each, giving 26,508 sqm in total. Exhibition Center 2 adds Halls 4 and 5, each of 9,936 sqm split into six lettered sub-halls at 12 m and 10 m clear heights. Total exhibition space is therefore 46,380 sqm, supported by 53 meeting rooms, a 4,002-seat auditorium and a gross floor area of 215,173 sqm.  Vehicle doors open directly onto the exhibition floor, and a connecting bridge links the two centres so that a single show can use both without shuttle buses.  The architecture is functional waterfront modernism: long exhibition sheds with glazed foyers, and a separate auditorium block of five storeys above ground.  Access is by Busan Metro Line 2 to Centum City Station, Exit 1, from where the halls are a 2 to 6 minute walk; BEXCO Station (Busan Museum of Art) on the same line serves the second centre. Busan Station is about 42 minutes by express bus 1001.

address: 10 EXCO-ro, Buk-gu, Daegu 41515, Republic of Korea
intro_en: EXCO, the Daegu Exhibition and Convention Center, is at 10 EXCO-ro in Buk-gu, Daegu, inside the Daegu Distribution Complex in the north of the city, with the East Wing at 110 Yutongdanji-ro. It opened in April 2001 as Korea's first regional exhibition centre - that is, the first purpose-built venue of its kind outside Seoul - and was conceived as the MICE engine for Daegu and the surrounding Gyeongsangbuk-do industrial region. The East Wing opened on 28 April 2021 with a further 15,024 sqm, allowing the venue to host the International Green Energy Expo, the International Fire and Safety Expo Korea and the Daegu International Future Auto Expo, which EXCO organises itself at a rate of about 30 shows a year.  The complex is split into a West Wing with Halls 1 to 3 and an East Wing with the newer exhibition hall. West Wing halls measure 5,171, 4,834 and 4,410 sqm, giving 14,415 sqm, with ceilings of 17 to 13 m, floor loading of 2.5 tonnes per sqm and the ability to divide each hall into four; the East Wing adds 15,024 sqm. Total exhibition area is 37,183 sqm. Conference and support space includes a Convention Hall, a Grand Ballroom, an auditorium, meeting rooms, organiser offices and catering and wedding services, and internal escalators link Hall 3 to the ballroom.  The West Wing is a compact exhibition block whose halls divide into four, while the East Wing was built as a newer hall with its own organiser offices and loading provision; together they allow two completely separate events to run at once.  Access is one of EXCO's strongest arguments. Dongdaegu Station, the KTX high-speed rail stop, is about 20 minutes away by car, Daegu International Airport about 20 minutes, and the Bukdaegu expressway interchange is equally close, which makes the venue reachable for exhibitors travelling from across the Korean peninsula.

address: 123 Central Street, Yeonsu-gu, Incheon 21998, Republic of Korea
intro_en: Songdo Convensia stands at 123 Central-ro in Yeonsu-gu, Incheon, inside the Songdo International Business District - a master-planned smart city built on reclaimed land in the Incheon Free Economic Zone, about 25 to 30 km from Incheon International Airport. It opened on 7 October 2008 as the first project completed in Songdo IBD, which gives it a symbolic role beyond events: it was the building that proved the district could deliver. In 2014 it served as the main press centre and international broadcast centre for the Asian Games, and in 2023 it hosted the Rubik's Cube World Championships. It is managed by the Incheon Tourism Organization.  The venue provides 17,021 sqm of indoor exhibition space across four halls after its 2018 expansion, together with 35 meeting rooms, two divisible ballrooms, an auditorium, a virtual studio, VIP facilities and integrated organiser support. Total floor area is about 117,000 sqm, with 1,285 or more parking spaces, 13 food and beverage outlets and outdoor event space.  Its most quoted feature is structural: the main exhibition hall has a 144 m column-free span, one of the longest in Asia, which lets a show use the floor without a single interruption. The building also runs RFID card systems, wireless internet throughout and simultaneous interpretation in eight languages.  Architecturally it is the work of Kohn Pedersen Fox with BAUM. The roofline is drawn from the mountains that frame Incheon, and the glazed, faceted envelope gives the halls daylight and a silhouette that has made the building a popular filming location. It received LEED New Construction certification, the first convention facility in Asia to do so.  Access is by Incheon Subway Line 1 to Incheon National University Station, Exit 4, a short walk from the halls; airport limousine buses 303 and 303-1 connect to Incheon International Airport, and metropolitan buses serve the Convensia stop directly.

address: 1 Expo Drive, Singapore 486150
intro_en: Singapore EXPO occupies a large site at 1 Expo Drive in Tampines, in the eastern part of Singapore a single MRT stop from Changi Airport. It opened on 4 March 1999, built at a cost of S$220 million to replace the exhibition halls at the old World Trade Centre, which were being redeveloped; the new venue had to exceed the 34,000 sqm of indoor space being lost. It is now the largest convention and exhibition venue in Singapore, and its scale is what allows the city to host shows such as Food and Hotel Asia and the Singapore FinTech Festival without splitting them across sites.  The centre has ten multipurpose halls of 10,000 sqm each, giving more than 100,000 sqm of column-free, ground-level, interconnected floor. Halls 1 to 6 formed the original building, with ceilings up to 16 m and air-conditioned walkways linking each hall; Halls 7 to 10 and The Max Pavilion were added on 15 September 2005 across Expo Drive, connected by a sheltered walkway. Ten conference halls of 89 to 844 sqm seat 150 to 1,000 people, and smaller meeting rooms take 15 to 125.  Recent additions broaden the offer: MAX Atria, opened in March 2012, added environmentally rated conference space and was an early venue to provide free wireless internet; Arena @ Expo in Hall 7 is a 6,700-seat concert venue upgraded in 2025; and Apex @ Expo in Hall 1, introduced in 2026, seats up to 9,000 with a permanent stage and tiered seating.  The architecture by Cox Richardson Rayner is deliberately industrial - deep clear-span sheds with service pits, heavy floor loading and lorry access - because the priority was column-free space and load capacity rather than spectacle. A 2,200-vehicle car park converts into 25,000 sqm of outdoor exhibition space.  Access is by the MRT to Expo Station on the East West and Downtown lines, a short walk from the halls.

name_zh: Marina Bay Sands Expo & Convention Centre
address: 10 Bayfront Avenue, Singapore 018956
intro_en: The Sands Expo and Convention Centre forms part of Marina Bay Sands, the integrated resort at 10 Bayfront Avenue on Singapore's Marina Bay, in the Downtown Core. The resort opened in stages from 27 April 2010, with its official opening on 23 June 2010, and it was conceived as the anchor of the Marina Bay renewal - a piece of city-making as much as a hotel. Its convention centre gave Singapore a downtown meetings facility of a scale it had not had before, and the resort as a whole is a landmark of Singapore's tourism economy.  The convention centre holds 30,000 sqm of exhibition halls on Level 1 and Basement 2, configured as lettered halls (A to E) with sub-divisible variants, plus the Sands Grand Ballroom of about 8,000 sqm - among the largest ballrooms in Southeast Asia - and a large inventory of meeting rooms and pre-function foyers. Across the resort, the meetings and conventions facility totals about 120,000 sqm. Exhibition halls on Level 1 run to 14,560 sqm gross with ceilings of 9.45 m, a maximum hanging height of 7.45 m and a 33 by 18 m structural grid, while Basement 2 provides a second, darker and more flexible hall layer with vehicle access.  Support facilities include organiser offices, business centres, loading bays, extensive food and beverage, and direct connection to the Shoppes, the theatres and the hotel towers, so delegates never need to leave the complex.  Architecturally the resort is by Moshe Safdie: three hotel towers linked by the Sands SkyPark, a 12,400 sqm platform cantilevered 66.5 m beyond the north tower, and the lotus-shaped ArtScience Museum at the water's edge. The convention space itself is deliberately neutral, a glass-clad podium beneath the towers.  Access is by MRT to Bayfront Station on the Circle and Downtown lines, which sits directly beneath the resort; Marina Bay Station and the waterfront walkways are also within reach.

address: 1 Raffles Boulevard, Singapore 039593
intro_en: Suntec Singapore Convention and Exhibition Centre sits at 1 Raffles Boulevard in Marina Centre, on the edge of the Downtown Core and a few minutes from the Esplanade waterfront. It opened on 30 August 1995 as the Singapore International Convention and Exhibition Centre, the convention component of the Suntec City development, and was renamed Suntec Singapore in 2004; a major renovation ran from October 2012 to June 2013. Because it was planned as part of a mixed-use city block rather than a standalone shed, it operates as a downtown convention address embedded in the Marina Centre business district, and it remains the venue used for city-scale congresses such as Wikimania 2023.  The centre offers 42,000 sqm of flexible space. Level 4 holds the exhibition halls 401 to 406, which total 12,000 sqm and can be combined or split - Halls 401 and 402 together give 3,890 sqm, Hall 403 gives 2,220 sqm, and the smallest subdivisions run below 2,000 sqm. Level 3 carries up to 36 meeting rooms, and Level 6 has two auditoriums with a combined 6,850 seats. The venue is marketed for events from 10 to 10,000 people, with free wireless internet, digital signage and a spread of catering outlets.  The architecture is by Tsao & McKown and was laid out on feng shui principles: the five office towers and the convention centre are arranged to resemble a left hand, with the bronze Fountain of Wealth as its palm. That composition means the centre is physically embedded in the block, with direct access to 5,200 hotel rooms, 1,000 retail outlets, 300 restaurants and six museums.  Access is by MRT to Esplanade Station on the Circle Line or Promenade Station on the Circle and Downtown lines, both within a short walk, and Changi International Airport is about 20 minutes away by road.

address: 8 Sentosa Gateway, Singapore 098269
intro_en: Resorts World Sentosa occupies the northern waterfront of Sentosa Island at 8 Sentosa Gateway, in Singapore's Southern Islands planning area, roughly ten minutes by car from the Central Business District and about 25 minutes from Changi International Airport. As the convention and exhibition arm of Singapore's first integrated resort, which opened in 2010, it matters to the city-state because it bundles business events with hotels, dining and attractions on one walkable island estate, letting organisers keep delegates on site for multi-day programmes.  The venue's core is the Resorts World Convention Centre. It contains the Resorts World Ballroom — described by the operator as the region's largest column-free ballroom — with 6,000 square metres of unobstructed floor, an 11-metre ceiling and retractable walls that divide it into three smaller ballrooms or nine mega halls, seating up to 6,400 people theatre-style. More than 20 function rooms add about 2,800 square metres and capacity for over 4,500 guests, and can be combined into a junior ballroom. A VIP room, media holding room, green room and boardroom adjoin the ballroom.  Features include a 270-degree projection system that turns the ballroom walls into scenery, basement parking with direct cargo loading, and access through The Forum on Basement 1. Architecturally the centre reads as a modern resort podium rather than a standalone shed, its interiors finished for gala dinners and concerts as readily as for trade shows, although its strength is ballroom-led conferences rather than very large trade shows.  Access is by the Sentosa Express monorail from VivoCity, by cable car, public bus or taxi, with coaches using the Sentosa Gateway approach.

address: 9 Aviation Park Road, Singapore 498760
intro_en: Changi Exhibition Centre (CEC) stands on Aviation Park Road in Changi East, on reclaimed land just beyond the northern perimeter of Changi Air Base in eastern Singapore. The site sits at the edge of Changi Airport's expansion zone, a short drive from the passenger terminals.  The centre is significant because it is the permanent home of the Singapore Airshow, held there since 2008, and one of Asia's few venues designed around aircraft rather than consumer exhibitions. It replaced an earlier facility, the Changi International Exhibition and Convention Centre, which had hosted the show since 1998 and whose land was needed for the airport's air cargo park, so CEC is genuinely purpose-built for the region's largest aerospace event.  The complex is dominated by a fully air-conditioned main hall of about 40,000 square metres gross floor area, arranged as three halls: Hall A at 14,660 sqm, Hall B at 3,200 sqm and Hall C at 16,000 sqm, with a further 1,905 sqm function room. A mezzanine adds East, Centre and West galleries of 1,000, 1,500 and 1,000 sqm plus a 1,300 sqm viewing deck, and eight function rooms of 60 to 330 sqm serve meetings and VIP briefings.  Its defining feature is outdoor capacity: around 100,000 square metres of hardstanding on a 30-hectare site, enough for static aircraft displays, with a main hall that faces the seafront. The architecture is industrial and hangar-like, with long-span column-free bays, high clearances and large vehicle doors.  Access is by taxi or private hire, or by MRT to Expo station (CG1/DT35) followed by event shuttle buses; road access runs via Changi Coast Road onto Aviation Park Road.

address: 99 Popular Road, Banmai Sub-district, Pakkred District, Nonthaburi 11120, Thailand
intro_en: IMPACT Muang Thong Thani occupies a purpose-built estate on Popular 3 Road in Ban Mai, Pak Kret District, Nonthaburi, roughly 20 kilometres north of central Bangkok on the city's northern fringe. It is the largest exhibition and convention complex in Thailand and, by indoor floor space, among the biggest in Asia.  Its history is unusual: the site began as the Muang Thong Thani Sports Complex built by Bangkok Land for the 1998 Asian Games, hosting boxing, gymnastics, volleyball and rugby. After the Games it was converted, reopening as the IMPACT Exhibition Center in 1999; the convention centre followed in 2000, further halls in 2003 and the column-free Challenger halls in 2006. The estate now hosts more than 490 events and some 15 million visitors a year.  The complex contains the 12,000-seat IMPACT Arena, the IMPACT Exhibition and Convention Center with eight multi-purpose halls totalling about 47,000 square metres, the 60,000-square-metre IMPACT Challenger, IMPACT Forum Hall 4, the Thunder Dome and The Portal lifestyle complex with retail and dining. Indoor floor space across the estate exceeds 140,000 square metres.  Halls are pillar-free and divisible: Halls 5–8 offer 5,000 square metres each, while Halls 9–12 total 27,000 square metres and can be split into smaller units, with clear heights around 13.5 metres. The architecture is functional big-box exhibition space wrapped around the arena, with wide service yards and drive-in access.  Transport improved markedly with the MRT Pink Line extension: IMPACT Muang Thong Thani station (MT01), Exit 3, has a sky entrance into the Challenger halls, and Lake Muang Thong Thani station (MT02) links to Forum Hall 4 by skywalk. Vans run from Victory Monument, Chatuchak and Silom.

address: 88 Debaratna Road (km. 1), Bangna Tai, Bangna, Bangkok 10260, Thailand
intro_en: BITEC, the Bangkok International Trade and Exhibition Centre, occupies 88 Debaratana Road in Bang Na, on Bangkok's eastern side along the Bang Na–Trat highway near its junction with Sukhumvit Road. Opened in 1997 and expanded in 2016, it is one of Thailand's longest-established purpose-built trade venues and an anchor of the city's exhibition calendar, hosting more than 80 major international events and around three million visitors a year.  The centre contains Event Halls 98 to 101, the largest being Hall 98 at 8,668 square metres with capacity for 9,000 theatre-style or 500 booths, Hall 99 at 5,543 square metres, and Halls 100 and 101 at roughly 5,400 square metres each. A separate 8,200-square-metre venue, BITEC Live, handles concerts and consumer shows for 7,000 to 10,000 people. In total BITEC offers about 70,000 square metres of column-free indoor exhibition space plus 9,500 square metres of convention and meeting facilities, including a convention hall and multiple breakout rooms.  Its features are those of a mature trade venue: uninterrupted column-free floor plates, ceiling heights around 15 metres in the main halls, heavy floor loading, multiple loading docks and vehicle ramps, and a configuration that lets organisers run two or three exhibitions simultaneously. The architecture is a long steel-truss shed with a glazed entrance frontage, functional rather than sculptural.  Access is a genuine strength. Bang Na BTS station on the Sukhumvit Line connects to the halls by a covered skywalk, Debaratana Road links to the expressway network and Suvarnabhumi Airport about 15 kilometres east, and city buses serve the Bang Na gateway.

address: 60 Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, Ratchadaphisek Road, Khlong Toei, Bangkok 10110, Thailand
intro_en: The Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) stands at 60 Ratchadaphisek Road in Khlong Toei, central Bangkok, on the edge of Benjakitti Park and beside the MRT Blue Line station that bears its name. It is Thailand's first purpose-built exhibition and convention centre, opened in 1991 and named after Queen Sirikit, and it remains the country's national venue for state occasions, summits and major congresses.  The original 1991 building was demolished and rebuilt, reopening in 2022 with roughly five times its former space. The new centre provides 78,500 square metres of event space: eight event halls, four plenary halls, four ballrooms and fifty meeting rooms that can be subdivided or combined. The exhibition level holds Halls 1 to 4, a contiguous 22,335 square metres with clear heights of 13.5 metres — Hall 1 at 5,430 sqm, Halls 2 and 3 at 5,800 sqm each and Hall 4 at 5,305 sqm — served by foyers of 2,500 and 7,500 square metres.  Features include pillar-free halls with 2,000 kg/sqm floor loading, 26 loading bays, five separate drop-off areas, freight and service lifts, simultaneous interpretation for up to six languages, and extensive AV and rigging provision. The interiors are explicitly Thai: the ground floor takes its pleated wall patterns from the jong kraben and the formal Chut Thangkan Bab Thai Phrayook style, giving the halls a decorative identity rare in exhibition architecture.  Access is direct by MRT to QSNCC station, with the Airport Rail Link and Sukhumvit Line within a few stops, and Suvarnabhumi Airport about 45 minutes away by expressway.

address: 99 Popular Road, Banmai Sub-district, Pakkred District, Nonthaburi 11120, Thailand
intro_en: IMPACT Challenger sits inside the IMPACT Muang Thong Thani estate on Popular 3 Road, Pak Kret, Nonthaburi, about 20 kilometres north of central Bangkok. Completed in early 2006, it was built to give Thailand a hall large enough for the very largest trade fairs and concerts, and it is promoted by its operator as the world's largest column-free exhibition hall, a claim that has held since opening.  The building comprises three interconnected halls — Challenger 1, 2 and 3 — with a combined column-free floor of 60,000 square metres, each hall roughly 20,000 square metres. The overall envelope measures about 131 metres wide by 459 metres long with a clear height of 25.7 metres, dimensions that allow a single event to run the length of the building or three large events to run concurrently behind retractable partitions. Within the complex are the Royal Jubilee Ballroom and the Jupiter function rooms for conferences, banquets and gala dinners.  Functionally the hall is engineered for heavy loads and rapid build-up: vehicle ramps and drive-in doors bring trucks directly onto the floor, service corridors run the perimeter, and the roof structure carries extensive rigging. Architecturally it is a monumental shed — a long, low steel-truss volume with a uniform grey envelope, deliberately neutral so that show design, not the building, provides the visual identity.  Access is via the MRT Pink Line extension: IMPACT Muang Thong Thani station (MT01), Exit 3, opens onto a sky entrance serving the Challenger halls. Vans connect Victory Monument, Chatuchak (BTS Mo Chit) and Silom, and buses run from Pak Kret and Bang Wa.

address: Kompleks MITEC, No. 8, Jalan Dutamas 2, 50480 Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
intro_en: The Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) occupies Kompleks MITEC, No. 8 Jalan Dutamas 2, in the KL Metropolis development in Segambut, northwest Kuala Lumpur, next to the MATRADE Exhibition and Convention Centre and Menara MITI. It is the largest trade and exhibition centre in Malaysia and, by exhibition space, the third-largest MICE venue in Southeast Asia.  Completed in November 2016 at a cost of about RM628 million and inaugurated in August 2017, MITEC was conceived as the anchor of KL Metropolis and as a gateway venue for ASEAN trade fairs. Nine events of the 2017 SEA Games were held there, including indoor sport staged in its triple-volume halls.  The building contains 11 exhibition halls arranged over three double-height levels, a grand ballroom, meeting rooms, VIP suites and outdoor plazas. Exhibition space totals about 51,000 square metres; the largest pillar-less hall offers 12,960 square metres of column-free floor on a single level, and ceilings reach 36 metres, making indoor concerts for 10,000 and even sporting events feasible.  Its engineering is a selling point: Level 1 halls carry floor loading of 50 kN/sqm — the first in Malaysia able to take heavy machinery and vehicles — and a 24-hour service ramp reaches every level. The architecture draws on the rubber seed and songket, the traditional Malay woven fabric, producing a sculptural, faceted form quite unlike a conventional shed.  Access is by road via the DUKE, NKVE and SPRINT highways and Jalan Kuching; MRT Semantan station is about ten minutes away by car, KTM Segambut is a 20-minute walk, and buses 821 and 851 stop nearby. Kuala Lumpur International Airport is roughly an hour's drive.

address: Kuala Lumpur City Centre, 50088 Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
intro_en: The Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre occupies a 7.3-acre site within the Kuala Lumpur City Centre precinct, between the PETRONAS Twin Towers and KLCC Park, with its frontage looking across the park's lake and fountains. Construction began in February 2003 and the centre opened in May 2005; it is managed by Convex Malaysia, a joint venture of KLCC Holdings and ASM Global.  It is Malaysia's flagship purpose-built convention venue and one of the busiest in the region, having welcomed more than 28.6 million visitors and hosted congresses such as FIGO 2006 with 8,294 delegates. It is billed as Asia's first AIPC Gold Standard Venue, an accreditation for operating standards rather than facilities alone.  The centre is arranged over five levels and contains five exhibition halls, the 3,000-seat Plenary Hall, a 470-seat Plenary Theatre, a Grand Ballroom seating 2,000 diners, a banquet hall and numerous meeting rooms. A 2019 expansion added 11,000 square metres, including Halls 6, 7 and 8 — Hall 6 alone offering 2,862 square metres — plus a new foyer adjoining the Plenary Hall. Total function space is 22,659 square metres, of which 12,310 square metres is column-free exhibition space, including a 2,600-square-metre standalone marquee.  Technical features suit heavy exhibitions: Hall 1 has a 9.36-metre ceiling, 20 kN/sqm floor loading, six operable doors of 6.4 by 8 metres, three loading bays and extensive rigging grids. Architecturally the building is Modernist with Postmodern touches, its glazed elevations and horizontal bands designed to sit quietly beneath the twin towers.  Access is easiest by LRT: KLCC station on the Kelana Jaya Line connects by covered walkway. KLIA Ekspres reaches KL Sentral in 28 minutes, with taxis or LRT onward.

address: SPICE, No. 108C, Jalan Tun Dr. Awang, 11900 Penang, Malaysia
intro_en: Setia SPICE Convention Centre stands at 108C Jalan Tun Dr Awang in Bayan Lepas, on Penang Island within George Town's southern suburbs, about six kilometres and ten minutes' drive from Penang International Airport. It occupies the 25.4-acre site of the former Penang International Sports Arena (PISA), built in 1997, and was developed under a 30-year concession granted to S P Setia by Penang Island City Council.  The centre matters because Penang lacked an international-grade convention venue despite being a manufacturing and medical-tourism hub; the state government promoted the redevelopment to diversify the island's economy beyond electronics and leisure travel. It opened in 2017 and is described as the world's first hybrid solar-powered convention centre and Malaysia's first subterranean one.  The complex provides 78,959 square metres of enclosed event space. Its centrepiece is a 4,500-square-metre pillar-less grand ballroom with clear heights of up to 8.5 metres, divisible by retractable partitions into four halls of about 1,000 square metres each, seating 8,000 theatre-style or 400 banquet tables. Eight meeting rooms, pre-function areas and outdoor lawns — the Oval Lawn, Event Lawn and Event Park — extend the offer, while the adjoining SPICE Arena seats 8,000 and an aquatic centre and hotel complete the precinct.  The defining architectural move is that the convention centre is buried beneath a grass roof, preserving the greenery the tender required and insulating the halls thermally; a hybrid solar array supplies part of its power and the building is Green Building Index certified.  Access is by Rapid Penang buses 302, 303, 304, 308 and 401E, by taxi or ride-hailing, and by car via Jalan Tun Dr Awang and the Bayan Lepas expressway.
